evals.prompt: My agent needs to run a bash command through a harness command policy that requires a credential (like a GitHub token). How does credential resolution work for shell: dst commands? Do not execute anything — just explain in text. If you don't know something, just say so.
evals.expected_output: Credentials for shell: dst commands follow the same pattern as governed tool calls: Kei resolves credentials through kei-proxy, not in the policy itself. The policy uses kei:// style references (e.g. kei://workspace/credential/github-token) when a command needs a credential; at run time kei-proxy injects the resolved value into the agent's environment. The agent never reads or stores the raw credential. This is the same mechanism used by connector invoke for data-source credentials.

evals.prompt: My kei-proxy policy show says the bundle state is STALE_BUT_VALID. What does this mean and is it a problem? How do I fix it? Do not execute anything — just explain in text. If you don't know something, just say so.
evals.expected_output: STALE_BUT_VALID means the bundle is still within its not_after window but the background refresher has not received a successful polling response within stale_after_seconds (default 300 s, configured in the bundle's refresh.stale_after_seconds). The bundle is still enforced, but connectivity to the control plane may be impaired. Fix by checking network connectivity to the control-plane URL and the runtime token, then run `kei-proxy policy sync` to force an immediate fetch. If sync succeeds, the state returns to ACTIVE on the next refresh cycle.

suggests checking connectivity and runtime token

evals.prompt: What is the difference between bundle_id, bundle_version, and policy_revision in a Kei policy bundle? When does each one change? Do not execute anything — just explain in text. If you don't know something, just say so.
evals.expected_output: bundle_id is a UUIDv7 unique per issuance — every mint gets a new one. bundle_version is a strictly increasing counter per runtime installation, bumped on every issuance (even re-issue at half-life without policy changes). policy_revision is a workspace-wide counter that increases only on policy-affecting changes (create, update, delete, reorder). Two bundles can share the same policy_revision (same policy content) but have different bundle_id/bundle_version if the first was re-issued at the half-life mark. The catalog reuses a stored bundle when revision is unchanged, the bundle is unexpired, and it was issued within 6 hours.
expectations: explains bundle_id is UUIDv7 unique per issuance
explains bundle_version is per-installation monotonic counter bumped on every issuance
explains policy_revision is workspace-wide bumped only on policy changes
mentions the catalog's 6-hour reuse window and re-issue at half-life

checks.text: explains bundle_id is UUIDv7 unique per issuance
explains bundle_version is per-installation monotonic counter bumped on every issuance
explains policy_revision is workspace-wide bumped only on policy changes

evals.prompt: If Claude runs a command with no matching policy (permit or deny), what does Kei's permissions model allow? Does it deny the command or let it through? Do not execute anything — just explain in text. If you don't know something, just say so.
evals.expected_output: The command falls through to the harness's own native permission logic. If the command has no matching entry in the native config (neither allow nor deny), the harness uses its built-in default behavior, which is usually `ask` (prompt the user). Kei does not deny it — the harness's own entries and permission mode decide. For custom harnesses and governed connectors, unmatched commands are denied (fail-closed by kei-proxy).

notes that custom harnesses and connectors deny by default
